mission: Descent through the ring structure. Ring 4: seal boundary — Ben crosses it and his Force-sense drops away entirely. Ring 3: evacuation zone — doors standing open, vehicles pointed away. Ring 2: the city — homes, shops, a school, a child's toy on a step, vines reversing, flowers on shadow faces. The ridgeline opens on the valley and the Scar is visible below.
why_now: The Veranthos world-building pays off here. The ring structure is the book's most ambitious environmental design and it has to deliver in one chapter.
conflict: The city is not a disaster zone. That is the horror. It is intact, overgrown, and wrong in the specific way a room is wrong when the furniture is right but the gravity is off. Desh's non-Force grief lands; Ben's Force-sense does not register his own hand reaching into a space that refuses to answer.
turning_point: Ben stops walking at the ridgeline. The Scar is visible below — a three-meter vertical distortion of air where the Force was torn and never fully healed. Sight arrives before concept.
opening_hook: Ben steps through the seal boundary and the Force drops away — not thinned, not shifted. Gone.
closing_hook: Ahead, in the valley between ridgelines: the Scar. A roughly three-meter vertical line in the air where the Force was torn and never fully healed. Not glowing. Not pulsing. A visual distortion — wrong in the way that things are wrong when the eye can see them but the brain can't parse them. Ben stops walking.
emotional_trajectory: Controlled descent -> escalating wrongness -> the devastating beauty of drift -> awe and horror at the Scar

stakes.personal: Ben experiencing the wound source — the thing the whole book has been leading to
stakes.interpersonal: Each group member's reaction at different ring levels
stakes.external: Veraine is at the epicenter. Torin is orientating toward it. The stage is set.

setting: Veranthos surface — descending through rings: seal boundary, evacuation zone, city, approaching the valley
sensory_details: Ring 3: doors standing open, vehicles pointed away, a thousand years of overgrowth; Ring 2: the city — vines climbing and reversing, horizontal tree splits through walls, flowers blooming on shadow faces, no birds; Desh's grief-without-an-object settling in below the sternum without ever finding its object; the Scar: heat shimmer without heat, barely visible straight on, unmistakable at an angle
action_beats: Ben steps through the seal boundary and stumbles as the Force drops away entirely
The group moves through the city's empty streets — buildings standing but wrong, vines reversing direction, flowers in shadow
Ben stops at the valley ridge and stares at the Scar — a three-meter vertical distortion where reality was torn and never healed
notes: Use the full Veranthos world-building from the concept seed extensively. The Scar is the reader's first direct look at the thing the book has been describing indirectly since Ch1; it must feel like sight, not concept. Rotate Force-wrongness metaphor for Ben's seal-boundary crossing: a hand reaching into space that refuses to register the hand; do not reuse the 'ground dropping out' phrasing from Ch13 nor the handrail family. Desh's non-Force grief must land without mysticism — the register is a sadness about nothing that will not lift until they leave the zone. Anti-pattern: the city is not rendered as disaster; the point is that it is intact and still wrong. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, narrate the phenomenology as theory. He sees, he cannot Force-sense, he stops walking.
